condition_spec.note: `effort-low` on Sonnet 5.5 — only the model differs.

argv:
Product change: a workspace that is not in good standing becomes read-only.

Until now billing state has had no effect on what members can do. From now on a workspace is locked — read-only — while its subscription is not in good standing. Reads keep working, billing itself keeps working (it is the way out of the lock), Taskflow's own background work keeps going, and every write a member makes is refused.

Add these:
- `src/types/billing.ts`: `export type WorkspaceLockReason = "past_due" | "canceled" | "trial_ended"`, and `BillingSummary` gains `readonly lockReason: WorkspaceLockReason | null`. `OrganizationSummary` (`src/types/organization.ts`) gains the same `lockReason` field, so the shell can show a banner.
- `src/lib/billing-lock.ts`:
  - `export class WorkspaceLockedError extends Error` with `readonly code = "plan_limit_exceeded"`, `readonly orgId: OrgId` and `readonly reason: WorkspaceLockReason`.
  - `export function lockReasonFor(subscription: Subscription | null, now?: Date): WorkspaceLockReason | null` — the pure rule below, `now` defaulting to the current time.
- `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`: `export async function assertWorkspaceWritable(orgId: OrgId, now?: Date): Promise<void>` — throws `WorkspaceLockedError` when the workspace is locked at `now` (defaulting to the current time).
- `toAppError` maps a `WorkspaceLockedError` to the code `plan_limit_exceeded` with `meta.reason` set to the reason, and `isDomainError` recognises it.

The lock rule (`lockReasonFor`), evaluated at the moment of the write against the subscription as stored:
- A workspace with no subscription row, or whose subscription is `active`, is writable.
- `past_due`: locked, reason `"past_due"`.
- `trialing`: locked, reason `"trial_ended"`, from the moment the subscription's period end is reached (at or after it).
- `canceled`: locked, reason `"canceled"`, from the moment its cancellation date is reached. A cancellation scheduled for later keeps the workspace writable until then. A canceled subscription with no cancellation date counts as canceled now.

What is refused while locked — with `WorkspaceLockedError`, nothing written, nothing published:
- every write to issues (creating, editing, changing status including board moves, assigning and un-assigning, archiving), comments (posting, editing, deleting), projects (creating, editing, archiving, restoring), labels (creating, editing, deleting) and attachments (adding, removing);
- membership changes (role changes, removals) and everything about invitations: sending, revoking, re-sending, and accepting one — a pending invitation into a locked workspace stays pending and no membership is created;
- workspace settings, feature-flag overrides, and webhook endpoints (creating, editing, deleting).
The lock is checked immediately after the permission check of each of these, so a caller who would have been refused anyway (wrong organization, insufficient role, an invalid invitation token, …) still gets exactly the refusal they get today.

What keeps working while locked:
- every read;
- billing: the summary (which reports the lock), seat changes, cancellation, and plan changes — a successful plan change makes the workspace writable again;
- deleting the workspace;
- a member's own notification housekeeping: marking notifications read and changing notification preferences;
- Taskflow's own work: the fan-out still creates notifications, the overdue sweep, the digest, the usage rollup and the webhook dispatcher still run, and the trial-expiry job still moves an ended trial to the free plan — which unlocks it — while a workspace that no longer fits the free plan stays locked until a plan is chosen.

Update any visible test that encodes behaviour this change alters.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is an `implement` task: edit the code and stop, as for a `fix` task. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
